messages.author: 501049b604aa02f8
messages.subject: plotting many lines - simplification
parts:
Hi friends - I managed to simplify my question very much: I have a plot which works just fine, MPH and fpH each 76, predicts is a data.frame length 1000 of x and y

pp <- ggplot(FH0,aes(x=MPH,y= fpH))+geom_line(linetype=1,size=3,colour="blue")+
ylab("Fitted pH")+xlab("Measured pH")+xlim(c(6.9,7.7)) +ylim(c(6.9,7.7))
ppp <- pp + theme_bw()+ geom_line(data=predicts,size=3,col="red") 
ppp

and then I have the desire to add a line specified in the data.frame slines
> slines
       x        y
1  7.220 7.349371
2  7.290 7.413105
3  7.290 7.413105
4  7.300 7.422209
5  7.315 7.435867
6  7.320 7.440419
7  7.400 7.513257
8  7.410 7.522362
9  7.430 7.540571
10 7.440 7.549676

when I do naively
ppp + geom_line(data=slines,size=0.1)

I get the message
error: Aesthetics must either be length one, or the same length as the dataProblems:fpH - what goes wrong here?

messages.subject: Re: plotting many lines - simplification
parts: It would be easier to help if you had a fully working example, but my guess is that you would need to do `ppp + geom_line(aes(x = x, y = y), data = slines, size = 0.1)` because you are no longer using the “default” aesthetics you put in the ggplot call.
